title: Timber cranes
intro: KESLA timber cranes are most often mounted on a truck to handle timber, sorted by wood type or as whole trunks. They also suit bioenergy work, for example feeding a chipper, and fixed industrial use. The range has both straight-boom and Z-⁠boom cranes.
standard: KESLA cranes meet the EN 12999:2011 HC1/HD4/B4 standard.

items.title: In-boom hosing
items.text: In the new 21-series KESLA cranes the hoses run inside the booms, the transfer boom too. This cuts the risk of hose damage.

items.title: Space-saving Z-boom
items.text: Kesla offers a wide range of Z-boom cranes. Their transport position saves valuable load space.

items.title: New joint between the main and transfer booms
items.text: The new type of joint keeps the hydraulic hoses well protected.

items.title: Wide-angle joint
items.text: Gives the best lifting capacity in every boom position.

items.title: V-shaped bottom of the transfer boom
items.text: Makes work with the grapple more precise.

items.title: KesLINK link
items.text: The KesLINK link, invented by Kesla, protects the hoses that lead to the grapple.

items.title: Wide choice of control valves
items.text: Kesla offers both mechanical and electric control valves for its cranes.

items.title: Stabilizer and stabilizer cylinder options
items.text: Integrated, separate, extra wide, for chipper use or for stationary use. The choice depends on the model.

items.title: Top-seat equipment
items.text: Handy when loading and unloading are short. Besides the standard version there is a side version with a good view of the work, and an E version with a very small slewing radius.

items.title: The KESLA proG grapple range
items.text: Timber and bioenergy grapples in many sizes. The geometry is carefully planned, so one log or a big bunch is easy to grab. Durable materials give a long service life.

items.q: Can KESLA cranes be used for other work than timber loading?
items.a: Yes. KESLA cranes and loaders can handle lime, bioenergy, scrap, metal and firewood, among many others. Usually another kind of grapple is needed.

items.q: Is an electric control valve available?
items.a: Yes, for KESLA cranes with a cabin.

items.q: How does the central lubrication system work?
items.a: There are two options, mechanical and electric. The mechanical system feeds grease to the lines when the stabilizers are stretched out. The electric system is fully controlled from the cabin.

items.q: What cooling is available for KESLA proCAB cabins?
items.a: A cooler and air conditioning are optional. Where there is no room for cooling equipment, a ceiling fan is available.
